problem_text:
A logistics manager is selecting cargo containers to load onto a cargo plane. The available containers are:

* Container 1: weight 27 kg, revenue $196
* Container 2: weight 38 kg, revenue $288
* Container 3: weight 12 kg, revenue $56
* Container 4: weight 50 kg, revenue $70
* Container 5: weight 9 kg, revenue $216
* Container 6: weight 18 kg, revenue $53
* Container 7: weight 35 kg, revenue $158
* Container 8: weight 34 kg, revenue $95
* Container 9: weight 46 kg, revenue $252
* Container 10: weight 27 kg, revenue $135
* Container 11: weight 24 kg, revenue $150
* Container 12: weight 18 kg, revenue $178
* Container 13: weight 12 kg, revenue $142
* Container 14: weight 14 kg, revenue $60
* Container 15: weight 19 kg, revenue $207
* Container 16: weight 26 kg, revenue $183
* Container 17: weight 30 kg, revenue $58
* Container 18: weight 43 kg, revenue $45
* Container 19: weight 36 kg, revenue $134
* Container 20: weight 11 kg, revenue $244
* Container 21: weight 13 kg, revenue $194
* Container 22: weight 49 kg, revenue $146
* Container 23: weight 3 kg, revenue $79
* Container 24: weight 1 kg, revenue $198
* Container 25: weight 29 kg, revenue $156
* Container 26: weight 43 kg, revenue $299
* Container 27: weight 20 kg, revenue $178
* Container 28: weight 12 kg, revenue $17

The cargo plane has a maximum payload capacity of 489 kg. Select the combination of containers that maximizes total revenue without exceeding this weight limit. Each container must be either fully loaded or left behind.
